title: Sigiriya
summary: Sigiriya is a rock in central Sri Lanka with sheer cliffs rising as high as 180 m above the surrounding land. Sri Lanka's Central Province tourism site says King Kashyapa (477 to 495 AD) built his palace on top, and NASA describes a fifth-century palace and fortress on the flat summit. The site was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of Kashyapa's reign, 477 AD, per the Central Province tourism page; NASA says only fifth-century. The palace is the work of his reign, so the build dates are not separately stated. End is the present: the ruin stands.

as_recorded.value: King Kashyapa (477 – 495 AD) built his palace on top of this rock
Fifth-century king Kasyapa had a palace and fortress built on Sigirya's relatively flat summit.

where.historical_name: Sigiriya, the palace-fortress of King Kashyapa, Anuradhapura-period Sri Lanka

importance.justification: NASA notes UNESCO World Heritage designation in 1982.

reviewer_note: Outline only, no model: height 180 m is on both pages (NASA "as high as 180 meters", Central Province "approximately 180 metres"), but no plan dimension was found (the 140 x 40 m figure on the Central Province page is the painted rock face). UNESCO page was blocked (403). Palace dates are the reign of Kashyapa; the pages do not give the build years.
